name: bm-v4-junction-bending
claim: Junction bending — harmonic angle restraints pinned to each crosslink's as-formed geometry — is the constraint that governs the basement membrane's stiffness (bm-v3 showed crosslink connectivity alone cannot, z < 4). Adding it dominates the network's mechanics, but a CLEAN, reproducible elastic modulus is not obtainable at v1 network size.
experiment: Implement bending via LAMMPS `fix restrain` pinned to each junction's as-formed angle (a per-junction rest angle, so no single-rest-angle frustration), with an auto-reduced timestep for stability. Measure the ATHERMAL modulus by energy minimisation (change_box + minimise; deterministic, no thermal chaos) and sweep the bending stiffness bending_k.
result: The floppy baseline (bending_k = 0) is measured cleanly and reproducibly: E ≈ 0 (per-seed −0.006, 0.0, 0.015). Turning bending on produces a LARGE mechanical response (|E| jumps to tens–hundreds) — the network is no longer floppy — but the stiff, pre-stressed, disordered network has many near- degenerate minima, so the modulus is ILL-CONDITIONED: it scatters wildly and sign-flips (k=80 per-seed −570 … +54, median −210). FP1 therefore confirms bending's role qualitatively (it dominates the mechanics) but does NOT yet yield a calibratable modulus. A clean value needs a much larger network (self- averaging) and a pre-stress-free reference state — a scoped v2 task.

purpose.question: Does junction bending yield the measurable modulus the vertex model needs?
purpose.mechanism: Bending constraints at crosslink junctions lift a sub-isostatic (z < 4) central-force network out of the floppy regime — the physically-expected rigidity source for a semiflexible fiber network.
purpose.expected_outcome: A finite, positive modulus that rises with bending stiffness. Observed: a large response, but not a reproducible modulus at v1 size.

key_assumptions: Bending = harmonic angle restraint pinned to each junction's as-formed angle (fix restrain).
Stiff restraints need a reduced timestep (dt ≈ 0.002; the spec's own regime).
Athermal (T=0) energy minimisation gives the deterministic elastic modulus.

followup_proposals.title: Reproducible bending modulus at scale (larger network + pre-stress-free reference)
followup_proposals.motivation: The bending modulus is ill-conditioned at 200 rods. A 1000+-rod network self-averages the junction disorder, and minimising to a pre-stress-free reference before straining removes the pre-stress artefact — together they should yield a reproducible, positive modulus vs bending_k.
followup_proposals.hypothesized_mechanism: Self-averaging + a relaxed reference → a well-conditioned shear modulus.

resolved_uncertainties: Bending, not crosslink connectivity, governs this network's stiffness (confirmed qualitatively).
The athermal minimisation measures the floppy modulus cleanly (fixes the dynamic-measurement chaos).
remaining_uncertainties: A reproducible, calibratable bending modulus — blocked on network size + pre-stress-free measurement.

config.title: Simulation movie — rods pinned at crosslink angles

limitations: The bending modulus is ill-conditioned at 200 rods (pre-stress + finite-size); not calibratable yet.
Bending targets are pinned from a thermally-noisy as-formed geometry (a pre-stress source).
Only equibiaxial stress-strain slope is used; a shear or energy-curvature modulus may be better conditioned.

report.title: Stage v4 — junction bending: mechanism confirmed, modulus not yet calibratable
report.verdict: Junction bending is implemented and DOMINATES the network's mechanics (floppy E≈0 → |E| tens–hundreds), confirming it — not crosslink count — governs BM stiffness. But the modulus is ill-conditioned at v1 network size (sign-flipping scatter from pre-stress + near-degenerate minima), so it is not yet a calibratable input for the vertex model. Next: a larger network + a pre-stress- free reference (fp3).
report.main_insight: Bending is the right rigidity mechanism (and the athermal measurement cleanly nails the floppy baseline), but turning it into a reproducible modulus is a finite-size / pre-stress problem that needs a larger, relaxed network.
